entries.title: HTTP Error 500.30 - ASP.NET Core app failed to start
entries.signature: HTTP 500.30 ANCM In-Process Start Failure app failed to start kestrel
entries.cause: The ASP.NET Core Module (ANCM) could not start the app in-process. This is usually caused by an exception thrown during application startup (Program.cs / Startup.cs), a missing dependency, or a bad configuration value.
entries.solution:
1. Run the app directly from the command line with `dotnet YourApp.dll` to see the real startup exception.
2. Enable stdout logging in web.config (set stdoutLogEnabled="true") and inspect the log file.
3. Check Program.cs for exceptions thrown before the host runs (e.g. failing DI registrations, bad connection strings).
4. Ensure the correct .NET runtime is installed on the server.

entries.title: HTTP Error 500.31 - Failed to load ASP.NET Core runtime
entries.signature: HTTP 500.31 ANCM Failed to Find Native Dependencies runtime not found
entries.cause: The required .NET runtime version is not installed on the hosting machine, or the app targets a framework version that is missing.
entries.solution:
1. Install the .NET Hosting Bundle that matches your app's target framework on the server.
2. Verify installed runtimes with `dotnet --list-runtimes`.
3. Restart IIS with `net stop was /y` then `net start w3svc`.

entries.title: HTTP Error 500.19 - Internal Server Error (config)
entries.signature: HTTP 500.19 cannot read configuration file web.config aspNetCore module not installed
entries.cause: IIS cannot read the application's configuration (web.config), often because the ASP.NET Core Module is not installed or the web.config is malformed.
entries.solution:
1. Install the ASP.NET Core Hosting Bundle on the server.
2. Validate web.config XML for syntax errors.
3. Ensure the AspNetCoreModuleV2 is registered in IIS modules.

entries.title: Unable to resolve service for type while attempting to activate
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Unable to resolve service for type while attempting to activate controller constructor
entries.cause: A constructor requires a service that was never registered in the dependency injection container, so the framework cannot create the controller/class.
entries.solution:
Register the missing service in Program.cs before building the app, for example:
`builder.Services.AddScoped<IMyService, MyService>();`
Match the lifetime (AddSingleton / AddScoped / AddTransient) to how the service is used. For DbContext use `builder.Services.AddDbContext<MyDbContext>(...)`.

entries.title: Cannot consume scoped service from singleton
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Cannot consume scoped service from singleton lifetime mismatch
entries.cause: A singleton service depends on a scoped service. Singletons live for the whole app while scoped services live per-request, so this creates a captive dependency.
entries.solution:
1. Change the consuming service's lifetime to scoped, OR
2. Inject `IServiceScopeFactory` into the singleton and create a scope when you need the scoped service, OR
3. Inject `IServiceProvider` and resolve within a created scope.

entries.title: A possible object cycle was detected (JSON serialization)
entries.signature: JsonException A possible object cycle was detected object reference loop serialize navigation property
entries.cause: System.Text.Json tried to serialize an object graph with circular references (commonly EF Core navigation properties that reference each other).
entries.solution:
1. Configure the JSON options to ignore cycles:
`builder.Services.AddControllers().AddJsonOptions(o => o.JsonSerializerOptions.ReferenceHandler = ReferenceHandler.IgnoreCycles);`
2. Or return DTOs/ViewModels instead of EF entities.
3. Or use `[JsonIgnore]` on the back-reference navigation property.

entries.title: No database provider has been configured for this DbContext
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException No database provider has been configured for this DbContext UseSqlServer OnConfiguring AddDbContext
entries.cause: The DbContext was created without a configured provider. Either AddDbContext wasn't called, or the options weren't passed through the constructor.
entries.solution:
1. Register the context with a provider:
`builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(o => o.UseSqlServer(connectionString));`
2. Ensure your DbContext has a constructor `public AppDbContext(DbContextOptions<AppDbContext> options) : base(options) {}`.
3. If creating manually, override OnConfiguring with `optionsBuilder.UseSqlServer(...)`.

entries.title: A network-related or instance-specific error occurred (SQL Server)
entries.signature: SqlException network-related instance-specific error server not found not accessible connection string SQL Server
entries.cause: The app cannot reach the SQL Server instance: wrong server name, the service is stopped, the firewall blocks the port, or TCP/IP is disabled.
entries.solution:
1. Verify the connection string server name (use `(localdb)\MSSQLLocalDB` for LocalDB, `.` or `localhost` for a local instance).
2. Confirm the SQL Server service is running.
3. Enable TCP/IP in SQL Server Configuration Manager and open port 1433.
4. Test connectivity with `sqlcmd -S server -E`.

entries.title: Login failed for user (SQL Server)
entries.signature: SqlException Login failed for user authentication SQL Server integrated security password
entries.cause: Authentication to SQL Server failed: wrong credentials, the login lacks access to the database, or the wrong authentication mode is being used.
entries.solution:
1. Check the username/password in the connection string.
2. For Windows auth use `Integrated Security=true` (or `Trusted_Connection=True`).
3. Grant the login access to the database and a suitable role.
4. Confirm SQL Server allows the chosen authentication mode (Mixed vs Windows).

entries.title: There is already an open DataReader associated with this Connection (MARS)
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException open DataReader associated with this Connection MultipleActiveResultSets async await EF Core
entries.cause: Two queries ran on the same DbContext connection at the same time, usually due to a missing await, parallel queries, or lazy loading inside a loop over an active query.
entries.solution:
1. Always await EF Core async calls and never share a DbContext across concurrent operations.
2. Materialize the query with `.ToListAsync()` before iterating and issuing further queries.
3. As a workaround add `MultipleActiveResultSets=True` to the SQL Server connection string.

entries.title: Object reference not set to an instance of an object
entries.signature: NullReferenceException Object reference not set to an instance of an object null
entries.cause: Code dereferenced a variable that is null (e.g. calling a method or property on a null object).
entries.solution:
1. Find the exact line from the stack trace and check which reference is null.
2. Add null checks or use null-conditional operators (`obj?.Property`).
3. Enable nullable reference types (`<Nullable>enable</Nullable>`) to catch these at compile time.
4. For model binding, verify the request actually populated the expected object.

entries.title: InvalidOperationException: Unable to track an entity because its primary key is already tracked
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException instance of entity type cannot be tracked another instance same key value already being tracked
entries.cause: Two different entity instances with the same primary key are being tracked by the same DbContext, often from attaching/updating a detached entity that EF already loaded.
entries.solution:
1. Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only queries.
2. Fetch the existing tracked entity and update its values instead of attaching a new instance.
3. Use a fresh, short-lived DbContext per unit of work.
4. Detach the previously tracked entity before attaching the new one.

entries.title: CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present
entries.signature: CORS policy Access-Control-Allow-Origin header blocked cross-origin request UseCors AddCors
entries.cause: The browser blocked a cross-origin request because the server did not return the proper CORS headers, or CORS middleware is missing/misordered.
entries.solution:
1. Register a CORS policy: `builder.Services.AddCors(o => o.AddPolicy("AllowFront", p => p.WithOrigins("https://localhost:3000").AllowAnyHeader().AllowAnyMethod()));`
2. Add `app.UseCors("AllowFront");` BEFORE `UseAuthorization` and after `UseRouting`.
3. Do not combine `AllowAnyOrigin()` with `AllowCredentials()`.

entries.title: InvalidOperationException: Unable to find the required services. UseRouting/UseEndpoints
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Unable to find the required services AddRouting AddControllers middleware order UseRouting UseEndpoints
entries.cause: Required services or middleware are missing or in the wrong order in the request pipeline (e.g. UseRouting after UseEndpoints, or AddControllers not called).
entries.solution:
1. Ensure the correct order: `UseRouting()` -> `UseAuthentication()` -> `UseAuthorization()` -> endpoint mapping.
2. Call the matching `Add*` service registration (e.g. `AddControllers`, `AddRazorPages`).
3. In minimal hosting (.NET 6+) prefer `app.MapControllers()` after `app.UseAuthorization()`.

entries.title: 401 Unauthorized - authentication scheme not configured
entries.signature: 401 Unauthorized No authenticationScheme was specified DefaultChallengeScheme AddAuthentication JWT bearer
entries.cause: The app uses [Authorize] but no authentication scheme/handler is registered, or the token/cookie is missing or invalid.
entries.solution:
1. Register authentication, e.g. JWT:
`builder.Services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme).AddJwtBearer(opts => { ... });`
2. Add `app.UseAuthentication();` before `app.UseAuthorization();`.
3. Verify the client sends a valid `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header (correct issuer, audience, and not expired).

entries.title: Antiforgery token validation failed (400 Bad Request on POST)
entries.signature: antiforgery token could not be decrypted validation failed __RequestVerificationToken 400 form post
entries.cause: An MVC/Razor Pages form POST is missing or has an invalid antiforgery token, or the data protection keys changed (e.g. after a redeploy or in a load-balanced farm).
entries.solution:
1. Include `@Html.AntiForgeryToken()` (Razor Pages adds it automatically inside <form>).
2. For AJAX, send the token in the `RequestVerificationToken` header.
3. Persist Data Protection keys to a shared store (file system / Redis / Azure Blob) so they survive restarts and scale-out.

entries.title: The SSL connection could not be established / dev certificate not trusted
entries.signature: HttpRequestException The SSL connection could not be established dev certificate not trusted dotnet dev-certs https
entries.cause: The ASP.NET Core HTTPS development certificate is missing or not trusted on the machine.
entries.solution:
1. Trust the dev cert: `dotnet dev-certs https --trust`.
2. If problems persist, clean and regenerate: `dotnet dev-certs https --clean` then `dotnet dev-certs https --trust`.
3. For HttpClient-to-HttpClient calls in dev, ensure the target cert is trusted or configure the handler appropriately (never disable validation in production).

entries.title: Address already in use / Failed to bind to address (port in use)
entries.signature: IOException Failed to bind to address address already in use port EADDRINUSE kestrel listen
entries.cause: Another process is already listening on the port Kestrel is trying to bind (often a previous instance of the app that didn't shut down).
entries.solution:
1. Find and stop the process using the port (Windows: `netstat -ano | findstr :5000` then `taskkill /PID <pid> /F`).
2. Change the port in launchSettings.json or `app.Urls`/`--urls`.
3. Ensure prior debug sessions are stopped.

entries.title: InvalidOperationException: Sequence contains no elements (First/Single)
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Sequence contains no elements First Single LINQ query empty
entries.cause: `First()`, `Single()`, or `Last()` was called on an empty sequence.
entries.solution:
1. Use `FirstOrDefault()` / `SingleOrDefault()` and handle the null result.
2. Check `.Any()` before calling First/Single.
3. For `Single`, ensure the predicate matches exactly one element (use `SingleOrDefault` to allow zero).

entries.title: The view 'Index' was not found (Razor view discovery)
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException The view was not found searched locations Views Shared Razor MVC
entries.cause: MVC could not locate the Razor view file in any of the searched locations, often due to a wrong file name/path, missing Views folder, or returning a view name that doesn't exist.
entries.solution:
1. Confirm the .cshtml file exists under `Views/<Controller>/<Action>.cshtml` or `Views/Shared`.
2. Match the action's returned view name exactly (case-sensitive on Linux).
3. Ensure the view file's Build Action is `Content` and it is published.
4. For Razor Class Libraries, verify the RCL is referenced correctly.

entries.title: Configuration / connection string returns null (appsettings not loaded)
entries.signature: ArgumentNullException connection string null GetConnectionString appsettings configuration not loaded environment
entries.cause: A configuration value (e.g. connection string) is null because the key name is wrong, the appsettings file isn't copied to output, or the environment-specific file isn't being loaded.
entries.solution:
1. Read it via `builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Default")` and verify the key matches appsettings.json.
2. Ensure appsettings.json `Copy to Output Directory` is set appropriately (default web SDK already includes it).
3. Check `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` so the right appsettings.{Environment}.json is loaded.
4. Use User Secrets in development for sensitive values.

entries.title: 415 Unsupported Media Type when POSTing JSON to an API
entries.signature: 415 Unsupported Media Type FromBody Content-Type application/json model binding api controller
entries.cause: The request's Content-Type doesn't match what the action expects (commonly missing `Content-Type: application/json` with a `[FromBody]` parameter).
entries.solution:
1. Send the header `Content-Type: application/json` with the JSON body.
2. Ensure the action parameter is `[FromBody]` and the JSON shape matches the model.
3. Confirm `AddControllers()` is registered and the JSON formatter is available.

entries.title: 400 Bad Request - validation errors (ApiController ModelState)
entries.signature: 400 Bad Request validation errors ModelState ApiController automatic model validation required field
entries.cause: With `[ApiController]`, invalid ModelState automatically returns 400 with a ValidationProblemDetails body before your action runs.
entries.solution:
1. Inspect the response body 'errors' object to see which field failed.
2. Fix the request payload to satisfy the data annotations ([Required], [Range], etc.).
3. To customize behavior, configure `ApiBehaviorOptions.InvalidModelStateResponseFactory`.

entries.title: PlatformNotSupportedException / DllNotFoundException when running on Linux/Docker
entries.signature: PlatformNotSupportedException DllNotFoundException libgdiplus System.Drawing Linux Docker native library
entries.cause: Code uses a Windows-only API or a native library that isn't present in the Linux/Docker image (classic example: System.Drawing.Common).
entries.solution:
1. Replace Windows-only libraries with cross-platform alternatives (e.g. ImageSharp / SkiaSharp instead of System.Drawing).
2. Install the missing native package in the Docker image (e.g. `apt-get install -y libgdiplus`).
3. Check the docs of the failing API for platform support.

entries.title: AmbiguousMatchException: The request matched multiple endpoints
entries.signature: AmbiguousMatchException request matched multiple endpoints route template duplicate attribute routing
entries.cause: Two or more actions/endpoints match the same route template, so the router cannot choose one.
entries.solution:
1. Give each action a unique route template or HTTP method.
2. Avoid duplicate `[Route]`/`[HttpGet("...")]` attributes that resolve to the same path.
3. Use route constraints to disambiguate (e.g. `{id:int}`).

entries.title: EF Core migration: pending model changes / no migrations applied
entries.signature: PendingModelChangesWarning database operation expected to affect rows migrations Add-Migration Update-Database table does not exist
entries.cause: The database schema is out of sync with the EF Core model: migrations were not added or not applied to the database.
entries.solution:
1. Add a migration: `dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate`.
2. Apply it: `dotnet ef database update`.
3. In code you can call `db.Database.Migrate()` at startup for dev.
4. Ensure the EF Core tools package is installed (`dotnet tool install --global dotnet-ef`).

entries.title: StackOverflowException from infinite recursion / AutoMapper cyclic mapping
entries.signature: StackOverflowException infinite recursion stack overflow property getter setter recursive call
entries.cause: Code recurses without a base case, or a property getter/setter calls itself (common with auto-properties referencing themselves, or recursive object mapping).
entries.solution:
1. Inspect the repeating frames in the stack trace to find the recursion.
2. Add a proper base/exit condition.
3. For self-referencing property bugs, ensure the backing field is used, not the property itself.
4. For mappers, configure max depth / preserve references.

entries.title: NETSDK1045: The current .NET SDK does not support targeting .NET X
entries.signature: NETSDK1045 current .NET SDK does not support targeting newer version install SDK TargetFramework
entries.cause: The project targets a .NET version newer than the installed SDK supports.
entries.solution:
1. Install the matching .NET SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download.
2. Or lower the project's `<TargetFramework>` to a version your SDK supports.
3. Verify with `dotnet --list-sdks`.
4. Pin the SDK with a global.json if needed.

entries.title: CS1061: 'Type' does not contain a definition for 'Member'
entries.signature: CS1061 does not contain a definition for and no accessible extension method missing using namespace
entries.cause: The code references a member/method that doesn't exist on the type, often due to a missing using directive (for extension methods), a typo, or a missing NuGet/package reference.
entries.solution:
1. Check spelling and the actual type of the variable.
2. Add the required `using` namespace for extension methods (e.g. `using System.Linq;` or `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;`).
3. Ensure the NuGet package that provides the member is referenced.

entries.title: Headers are read-only, response has already started
entries.signature: InvalidOperationException Headers are read-only response has already started StatusCode cannot be set middleware
entries.cause: Code tried to modify the response status code or headers after the response body had already begun streaming to the client.
entries.solution:
1. Set status codes/headers before writing to the body.
2. In middleware, buffer or check `HttpResponse.HasStarted` before modifying headers.
3. Move exception/short-circuit logic earlier in the pipeline so it runs before the response starts.
